metrics.label: PRs merged
metrics.definition: Pull requests you authored that were merged in this period.
metrics.formula: |{ p ∈ AP : p.mergedAt ∈ period }|
metrics.goodRange: Context-dependent; 4–12 per 4 weeks is typical for product teams.
caveats: Team conventions (stacked PRs, monorepo vs many repos) change counts a lot.
Merges done by others still count — authorship is what matters.
metrics.antiGaming: Score saturates at 12 per 4 weeks; tiny PRs are not rewarded beyond the small-PR ratio; splitting PRs artificially raises review load for teammates (visible in their data).

metrics.label: PRs opened
metrics.definition: Pull requests you opened in this period (including drafts).
metrics.formula: |{ p ∈ AP : p.createdAt ∈ period }|
caveats: Not scored, so opening PRs never raises the score by itself.
metrics.antiGaming: Not scored, so opening PRs never raises the score by itself.

metrics.label: PR cycle time (median)
metrics.definition: Typical business hours from a PR being ready for review to being merged, for your PRs merged in this period.
metrics.formula: median({ businessHours(readyAt(p), p.mergedAt) : p ∈ AP, p.mergedAt ∈ period })
metrics.goodRange: < 24 h excellent, 24–72 h healthy, > 1 week worth a look.
caveats: Depends heavily on reviewers' availability and team process; long-running feature branches by design will look slow.
Draft time is excluded by design.
Durations use business hours (Saturday and Sunday excluded); holidays are not modelled.
metrics.antiGaming: Opening PRs as drafts until approval would shorten cycle time; mitigated because first-pass approval and teammates' review data stay visible, and the metric is only 30 % of one dimension.

metrics.label: Merge rate
metrics.definition: Of your PRs that were closed in this period, the share that were merged.
metrics.formula: M / (M + U), M = prs_merged, U = |{ p ∈ AP : p.mergedAt IS NULL ∧ p.closedAt ∈ period }|; n = M + U
caveats: Closing obsolete PRs is good hygiene; the band saturates at 90 % so abandoning nothing is not required for a full score.
metrics.antiGaming: The band saturates at 90 %, so never closing a PR earns nothing extra.

metrics.label: Small PR ratio
metrics.definition: Share of your merged PRs with 400 or fewer changed lines.
metrics.formula: |{ p ∈ AP_m : changedLines(p) ≤ 400 }| / |AP_m|; n = |AP_m|
caveats: Generated files, lockfiles, migrations and renames inflate changed lines; GitHub does not let us exclude them per file in v2.0.
PRs whose size GitHub did not report are left out of the sample.
metrics.antiGaming: Splitting a change into dependent PRs is genuinely good practice; trivially small PRs don't move other metrics.

metrics.label: Revert rate
metrics.definition: Share of your PRs merged in this period that were later reverted.
metrics.formula: |{ p ∈ AP_m : p.revertedAt IS NOT NULL }| / |AP_m|; n = |AP_m|
caveats: Reverts made by plain `git revert` without referencing the PR are not detected.
The value for a past period can rise later when a revert lands.
Reverts are sometimes rollbacks of healthy changes for unrelated reasons.

metrics.label: Median PR size
metrics.definition: Typical changed lines (added + deleted) of your PRs merged in this period.
metrics.formula: median({ changedLines(p) : p ∈ AP_m })
caveats: Context only; shown next to the small-PR ratio and never framed as output.
Lines of code are never a productivity signal.

metrics.label: First-pass approval
metrics.definition: Share of your merged PRs approved without any 'changes requested' review.
metrics.formula: |{ p ∈ AP_m : p.changesRequestedCount = 0 }| / |AP_m|
caveats: Strongly dependent on team review culture; not scored for that reason.

metrics.label: PRs reviewed
metrics.definition: Distinct pull requests by others that you reviewed in this period.
metrics.formula: |{ p ∈ RP : ∃ r ∈ RV, r.pullRequestId = p.id ∧ r.submittedAt ∈ period }|
caveats: GitHub records each reply in a review thread as a COMMENTED review; counting distinct PRs removes that inflation.
A PR reviewed in two periods counts once in each.
metrics.antiGaming: Saturates at 15 per 4 weeks; rubber-stamp approvals are visible in review depth.

metrics.label: Review turnaround (median)
metrics.definition: Typical business hours from being asked to review to submitting your first review, for reviews submitted in this period.
metrics.formula: median({ businessHours(r₁.reviewRequestedAt, r₁.submittedAt) : p ∈ RP, r₁ = first review in period, r₁.reviewRequestedAt IS NOT NULL })
caveats: Reviews without a recorded request (e.g. drive-by reviews) are excluded.
Team requests are attributed to you if you reviewed (team membership is not visible).

metrics.label: Review balance
metrics.definition: How your reviewing compares with your authoring: reviews ÷ (reviews + merged PRs).
metrics.formula: prs_reviewed / (prs_reviewed + prs_merged); n = prs_reviewed + prs_merged
metrics.goodRange: 0.4–0.7. Score saturates at 0.5 — reviewing more than you author is never penalised.

metrics.label: Time to first review (as author)
metrics.definition: Typical business hours your PRs waited for a first review from someone else.
metrics.formula: median({ businessHours(readyAt(p), p.firstReviewAt) : p ∈ AP, p.firstReviewAt ∈ period })
caveats: Measures your teammates' responsiveness more than yours — never scored; shown to help you spot bottlenecks.

metrics.label: Review depth (median)
metrics.definition: Typical number of comments you leave per PR you review.
metrics.formula: median over PRs in prs_reviewed of Σ (r.commentsCount + (r.hasBody ? 1 : 0)) for your reviews r in period
caveats: More comments are not inherently better; shown for self-reflection only.

metrics.label: Repositories reviewed in
metrics.definition: Repositories where you reviewed pull requests by others in this period.
metrics.formula: distinct repositoryId over PRs counted in prs_reviewed

metrics.label: Repositories contributed to
metrics.definition: Repositories where you committed, opened or merged a PR, or reviewed in this period.
metrics.formula: distinct repositoryId over { CM by authoredAt } ∪ { AP by createdAt } ∪ { AP by mergedAt } ∪ { RP with a review in period }
metrics.goodRange: 1–5 (more is not better beyond focus limits; score saturates at 5).
caveats: Not rate-normalised (breadth over a year naturally exceeds a month).

metrics.label: Two-way repositories
metrics.definition: Repositories where you both merged your own PRs and reviewed others' PRs in this period — a sign of shared ownership.
metrics.formula: |{ repo of p ∈ AP, p.mergedAt ∈ period } ∩ { repo of q counted in prs_reviewed }|

metrics.label: Repositories with merged PRs
metrics.definition: Repositories where at least one of your PRs was merged in this period.
metrics.formula: distinct repositoryId over AP_m

metrics.label: Active days
metrics.definition: Days in this period with at least one commit, PR opened or review.
metrics.formula: distinct local dates of { CM.authoredAt } ∪ { AP.createdAt } ∪ { RV.submittedAt } within the period
caveats: Not scored, to avoid rewarding always-on or weekend work.

metrics.label: Active weeks
metrics.definition: Share of the period's working weeks with at least one contribution.
metrics.formula: W = ISO weeks with ≥ 1 weekday inside the period; |{ w ∈ W with a contribution on a date in w ∩ period }| / |W|
caveats: Holidays and leave lower it.
One contribution per week is enough, so it rewards steadiness, not volume.
Scored inside the Delivery dimension.
metrics.antiGaming: One contribution per week is enough; more activity earns nothing extra.

metrics.label: Commits
metrics.definition: Commits you authored on default branches in this period (merge commits excluded).
metrics.formula: |{ c ∈ CM : c.authoredAt ∈ period }|
caveats: Commit granularity is a personal style; squash-merge teams show few commits. Never scored.

metrics.label: Longest active-week streak
metrics.definition: Longest run of consecutive active weeks within this period.
metrics.formula: longest run of consecutive active weeks (as in active_weeks_ratio) within the period
caveats: Shown as a milestone only; never scored.

metrics.label: Issues completed
metrics.definition: Issues assigned to you that were completed in this period.
metrics.formula: issues assigned to the user with completedAt ∈ period and status category = done
caveats: Requires Jira or Linear (v2.1).

metrics.label: Story points completed
metrics.definition: Story points of the issues you completed in this period.
metrics.formula: Σ storyPoints over issues_completed (null points ignored; n = issues with points)
caveats: Requires Jira or Linear (v2.1).

metrics.label: Issue cycle time (median)
metrics.definition: Typical business hours from starting to completing your issues.
metrics.formula: median(businessHours(startedAt, completedAt)) over issues_completed
caveats: Requires Jira or Linear (v2.1).
